title: External OBIS thermal indices increased the space-for-time transfer of Northeast US Shelf zooplankton, larval fish and trawl species in 1982-2023; the marine counter-case is not an index artefact
abstract: Question: campaign work found that community thermal composition follows only 3-24% of its spatial temperature gradient in terrestrial and freshwater systems. British butterflies seemed to follow 62%, but species temperature indices (STI) from the survey's own sites caused this, and European STIs gave 14%. Northeast US Shelf plankton (5-year ratios 0.78 and 0.55) is the main remaining counter-case, and it also used survey-internal STIs. Is it the same artefact? Method: we repeated the published estimator exactly and changed only the STI source. The external STI of a taxon is the mean World Ocean Atlas 2023 surface temperature of the OBIS cells where it occurs in the Atlantic and Arctic. Data: EcoMon tows 1982-2023 (22 zooplankton and 32 larval fish taxa) and, as a third assemblage, NEFSC bottom-trawl hauls 1982-2019 (105 species); OISST v2.1. Paired 3-year x 2-degree block bootstrap (400), taxon-shuffle nulls, leave-one-taxon-out, eight STI variants, an exact split of the internal STI into the part that the external niche predicts and a residual, and species-level trend tests. Results: external STIs increased transfer. 5-year ratios went from 0.74 to 1.24 (zooplankton), 0.55 to 0.69 (larval fish) and 0.22 to 0.40 (trawl species); trend ratios from 1.63 to 2.66, 0.90 to 1.19 and 0.52 to 0.70. The paired difference was above zero at all timescales in zooplankton and for trends in all assemblages. The external ratio was larger in every variant. The residual internal-STI part carried 19%, -16% and -28% of the trend (butterflies: 82%) but 49%, 19% and 10% of the spatial slope: internal STIs made the benchmark too steep. In SST units the external CTI trend was 0.88, 1.25 and 0.75 of the SST trend. Taxon trends rose with external STI (Spearman 0.60 zooplankton, 0.26 trawl; larval fish 0.45, interval includes 0). Conclusion: near-full marine transfer on this shelf is not an internal-index artefact, and it also occurs in long-lived trawl species. Limitations: one shelf; surface temperature only; OBIS effort bias and genus-level niches; zooplankton trend ratio above 1 shows the within-shelf benchmark is too narrow; trawl external trend not clearly above the shuffle null (p = 0.11).

citations.reason: Exact estimator and code re-used; its near-full plankton transfer survives, and increases with, external thermal indices.
Butterfly internal-STI artefact (82% of trend in the unpredicted part); the same test gives the opposite result on the shelf.
75-network synthesis used internal STIs; shelf results show internal STIs can bias ratios downward.
No generation-time effect inside the bird survey; long-lived trawl species also show high transfer here.
